headline: Preparedness is readiness for what might come—having plans, supplies, and skills before you need them
universal_truth: Prepare when you can, not when you must; the time to get ready is before you need to be
fun_facts: Most experts recommend having at least 72 hours of supplies ready for emergencies
People with emergency plans respond faster and more effectively during crises
Preparation reduces both the objective danger and the subjective panic during emergencies
discussion_questions: How prepared are you for likely disruptions in your life?
What would you wish you had ready if something went wrong tomorrow?

hook.script: Disasters rarely announce themselves. Power outages, accidents, job loss, health crises—they arrive suddenly. Preparedness means having plans, supplies, and skills before the moment arrives. The time to prepare is now, not when crisis hits.

cliff.script: We know we should prepare, but often don't. What's the real value of being ready before you have to be?

options.text: Preparation in calm times creates options in crisis—you can't buy insurance after the accident; readiness gives you resources when acquiring resources is impossible
options.response: Yes. During crisis, there's no time to prepare—only time to execute. What you prepared before determines what options you have during. Prepare while you can, not while you must.
Peace of mind matters, but the practical benefit is having options when you need them...

fact1.title: Calm-Time Advantage
fact1.script: Preparing during calm times is efficient—you can think clearly, gather resources, and plan thoroughly. Preparing during crisis is panicked, expensive, and often impossible.

fact2.title: Plans, Skills, Supplies
fact2.script: Preparedness has three components: plans (what to do), skills (how to do it), and supplies (what to use). All three matter. Missing any one creates vulnerability.

fact3.title: Proportional Preparation
fact3.script: Prepare proportionally to likelihood and consequence. Everyday disruptions are likely—be ready. Catastrophes are unlikely but severe—be somewhat ready. Don't over- or under-prepare.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Prepare when you can, not when you must. The time to get ready is before you need to be. Prepare now.

outro.script: That's Day 314. Tomorrow, we'll explore weighing what could go wrong—risk assessment. Until then, consider your preparedness for likely disruptions.

growTrack.title: Preparedness Check - What Are You Ready For?
growTrack.learning_objective: Assess and improve readiness for disruptions
growTrack.activity: What disruptions are reasonably likely in your life—power outage, job loss, illness, natural disaster? For each: Do you have a plan? Do you have skills? Do you have supplies? Identify gaps.
